subject: Expedited price alignment & SOW appendix for pilot expansion - MedLytics
messages:
From: Ben Harper <ben.harper@medlytics.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot expansion — capacity + pricing alignment (MedLytics)

Diego,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team is excited to move the pilot to the next phase. We need to add an additional 250 GPU-hours per month for the 30‑day expansion and want to lock in pricing for the pilot period before we start onboarding. Attached is a short SOW appendix that spells out the extra capacity and a draft budget.

Can you confirm:
- Whether the additional capacity can be covered under our existing order form or whether you prefer a short-term amendment/change order?
- A target effective date for the expanded pilot (we're hoping to start the week of Mar 1).
- Any procurement docs you need from our side for faster approval.

We'd like to avoid a lengthy legal loop if possible — is there a playbook for an expedited amendment?

Thanks,
Ben Harper
Head of Platform & Procurement
MedLytics

Attachments: MedLytics_SOW_Appendix_Request_20270214.pdf (attachment stub)

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Harper <ben.harper@medlytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot expansion — capacity + pricing alignment (MedLytics)

Ben — thanks for the note and the appendix. Happy to prioritize this so you can hit the Mar 1 start date. Quick answers up front:
- We can do a short-term change order (amendment to the existing order form) that covers the 30‑day expansion and any overage terms.
- If we get internal sign-off this week, we can set the effective date as Mar 1 and provision the additional capacity.
- From procurement, a PO referencing the existing order form number is ideal. If procurement prefers a single combined order, we can generate an amendment that attaches to the MSA.

I've looped in Laura (legal ops) to drive the redlines and Karthik (acct exec) to confirm pricing/discounting. Laura — Ben attached a proposed appendix; can you suggest a minimal redline strategy that keeps approval time under 72 hours? Karthik — any flexibility on the one‑month pricing tier for this pilot?

I'll also attach our standard short-form change order template for transparency.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cost_model_breakdown_20270215.xlsx (internal cost workbook, stub)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Harper <ben.harper@medlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot expansion — capacity + pricing alignment (MedLytics)

Diego / Karthik / Ben — reviewed the SOW appendix. Redlines and recommended approach below. I'm keeping the external thread so Ben has visibility. Key items: 

1) Change order vs. amendment: A short-form change order (one page) attaching to the active order form will be fastest for procurement. It should:
   - Reference MSA and original order form ID
   - Add 250 GPU-hours for 30 days (explicit SKU and price)
   - Specify start date (Mar 1) and end date (Mar 31), with clear overage rate after cap

2) Pricing: if we want to avoid larger procurement approvals, offer a pilot-specific one‑month promotional rate (5% off standard committed rate) in exchange for a PO by Feb 18. Karthik, confirm if 5% is acceptable.

3) Liability/data: keep the same MSA terms (no new data residency or SLA changes) — this avoids an escalation to the commercial legal team.

4) Execution: signatory on the change order can be the same authorized signers in the original order form; if they need DocuSign, I can prepare.

I've prepared a redlined draft (redlined_orderform_draft_20270216.pdf) with tracked changes that remove nonessential legal language and keep the notice/termination language intact. Ben — if you can confirm PO timing and whether DocuSign is acceptable, I'll fast-track the DocuSign packet.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlined_orderform_draft_20270216.pdf (redline stub)

From: Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@medlytics.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Feb 2027 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot expansion — capacity + pricing alignment (MedLytics)

Thanks, Laura — this looks straightforward. A couple of clarifications from procurement and legal here: 

- PO timing: procurement can issue a PO by close of business on Feb 18 if the change order is one page and we can send it over for signature immediately.
- Pricing question: the team prefers a fixed unit price rather than a percentage discount shown in the change order. Can you state the effective per-GPU-hour rate in the doc? That will speed internal approvals.
- Invoice timing: we need an invoice aligned to the start date (Mar 1) with billing to occur on the first monthly invoice following provisioning.

Ben and I would like to avoid re-running the MSA-level terms if possible. If Laura can convert the redlines to a one-page change order with a flat per-GPU-hour figure, procurement will sign the PO tomorrow.

On the DocuSign front — yes, DocuSign works for us.

Sara Holmes
VP, Operations
MedLytics

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Harper <ben.harper@medlytics.com>, Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@medlytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot expansion — capacity + pricing alignment (MedLytics)

Sara / Ben — great, appreciate the quick turn. Laura updated the draft to include a flat per-GPU-hour rate of $6.25 for the 250 GPU-hours during the 30-day window and removed any nonessential clauses. DocuSign packet is ready. Action items: 

- Ben/Sara: send PO referencing "Order Form OF-2025-129" by EOD Feb 18. Proc team can attach that to the DocuSign packet or confirm in the DocuSign comments.
- Laura: please load the one-page change order into DocuSign and include the HubSpot deal ID in the envelope description (DL-2027-0457).
- Karthik: confirm final billing code and invoice cadence so accounting can expect invoice on the first monthly invoice after Mar 1.

If we get the PO and DocuSign signature tomorrow, we'll provision capacity Mar 1 and set up a brief onboarding call Mar 2 to walk the MedLytics engineers through prefix caching and batching settings for the pilot.

Thanks all — will follow up once signed.

Diego Fernandez
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: change_order_onepage_MLX_20270218.pdf (DocuSign-ready stub)
